definitions: To remove something from a larger piece by cutting.
To stop eating or drinking something, usually to improve health.
To stop doing or using something.
To stop functioning (of an engine or machine).
To be naturally suited for a particular role or activity (often in the passive voice).
examples: She cut out the picture from the magazine.
I'm trying to cut out sugar from my diet.
You should cut out all the unnecessary expenses.
The editor decided to cut out that scene from the film.
The engine suddenly cut out on the motorway.
He's not really cut out for a job in sales.
pastTenses: cut out (past simple), have/has cut out (present perfect)
